blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes the development and deployment of BBR (Bandwidth Bottleneck and Round-trip propagation time), a new TCP congestion control algorithm by Google's make-tcp-fast project. BBR achieves 2-25x throughput improvements over the loss-based CUBIC algorithm, with even more significant gains (up to 133x) when TCP receive buffer sizes are increased. The algorithm is also deployed on YouTube servers, showing improved quality-of-experience metrics and reduced median RTT globally (53% average reduction, >80% in developing regions). The key insight is that BBR replaces loss-based congestion control with a model-based approach that estimates bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip propagation time to operate at Kleinrock's optimal point, avoiding bufferbloat and misinterpretation of loss as congestion. The paper highlights BBR's simplicity, efficiency, and effectiveness in real-world deployments.
